headline: Drink water first thing in the morning
body: A glass of water right after waking up jumpstarts your body. Think of it like charging your phone overnight!

headline: Fuel your muscles with lean protein
body: Protein is essential for muscle repair. Lean meats like chicken breast, turkey, or beef are highly bioavailable sources.

headline: Plant-based protein builds muscle too
body: Legumes, lentils, tofu, tempeh, and seitan are excellent high-protein plant sources to repair and grow your muscle fibers.

headline: Greek yogurt is a protein powerhouse
body: Yogurt and cottage cheese are rich in casein protein, which digests slowly and provides a steady release of amino acids.

headline: Rest days are just as important as workout days
body: Your muscles actually grow while you sleep and rest — not during the workout itself. Don't feel guilty for resting!

headline: Slow and steady wins the race
body: Showing up 3 days a week consistently for a year beats going every day for one month and burning out. Progress takes time.

headline: Any movement counts
body: A 20-minute walk, gentle stretching, or even gardening — it all helps your body get stronger and healthier.

headline: Sleep is your secret superpower
body: 7–9 hours of sleep helps your body heal, your memory sharpen, and your energy stay high the next day.

headline: Start small and build up
body: Even 5 minutes of exercise is better than nothing. You can always do more next time — the key is to start!

headline: Fiber keeps your energy stable
body: Eating fiber-rich foods like oats, apples, chia seeds, and broccoli slows digestion, preventing blood sugar spikes and crashes.

headline: Replenish sodium and potassium
body: When you sweat, you lose critical minerals. Bananas, coconut water, or a pinch of sea salt in your water help prevent cramping.

headline: Warm up dynamically before lifting
body: Prioritize arm circles, leg swings, and bodyweight squats before training. Static stretching should be saved for after workouts.
